page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

This server includes 1890 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the D32ds_v7 demonstrates strong performance across several domains. It achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-threaded operations, including bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core workloads, fall into the strong performance tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only large block speeds at 166.74 GB/sec and write speeds at 65.26 GB/sec.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-memory ratio and high-speed local storage, the D32ds_v7 is well-suited for database operations, web serving, and moderate-scale LLM inference tasks. The inclusion of AMX instructions provides hardware-level acceleration for vector and matrix computations without requiring a dedicated GPU. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a dense resource profile that balances compute power, memory, and local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for enterprise applications requiring consistent, non-burstable CPU performance.
